$comment: THE TOOL REGISTER — the declarative half of what this system can do to the world.
EXECUTION_LAYER.md §16.2 specified this as a first-class artifact; docs/LLD.md §6.2 designs it.
Before it existed, the drain queried exactly one effect kind, so an effect of any other kind was
accepted, stored and never executed — with every screen looking healthy. Registering a kind here
ONE FILE, not one file per tool, and deliberately. A serverless bundle cannot glob a directory at
runtime, so per-file tools would need an index someone must remember to update — the same
forgettable step that leaves a connector wired and invisible in the connections UI.
This file holds FACTS ABOUT a tool. The executor itself is bound in code, in
src/tools/executors.ts, because a string path cannot be statically bundled and a tool that
resolves at runtime fails in production rather than in CI. `npm run check:tools` asserts the two
class: 'effect' does NOT put a tool in a handler's tool set. Handlers emit effects; the drain
performs them. That inversion is what makes the approval gates structurally true, and no entry
